properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From StoryFlow's unnumbered rule A, clause (d): "A test never observed red proves nothing. Red-then-green, or mutate the fix and confirm the suite notices. A green suite says the tests pass — not that they would catch a regression."

⭐ THE EVIDENCE THAT THIS IS REAL IS ALREADY IN THIS GRAPH, AND IT IS THE SAME SHAPE THAT JUSTIFIED `subject` EARLIER TODAY. 51 of 191 Verifications contain the word MUTATION in their prose — "MUTATION-CHECKED FIVE WAYS, each failing exactly the tests that name it", "MUTATION-CHECKED against five seeded regressions", "WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIX: the four bug cases failed and all five counterweights passed". The discipline is being practised, carefully, by whoever writes these. IT IS BEING WRITTEN INTO FREE TEXT BECAUSE THERE IS NOWHERE ELSE TO PUT IT. Nothing can count it, query it, or notice its absence — which is the exact argument that carried `ChangeSubject`, one field over.

WHAT IT WOULD BE: a Verification records whether it has ever been observed FAILING — not as a status (status is now), but as a fact about its history. `set_verification_status(failing)` already exists, so the honest cheap version is derived rather than declared: has this check ever been written `failing`? On this design that answer is currently NO for essentially all 191, because a check is created and then set passing.

THREE FORMS, increasingly strong:
(a) DERIVED — compute "ever observed failing" from the status history. Free, no new vocabulary, and worth nothing here because the history does not exist: statuses are overwritten, not journalled.
(b) A FIELD the author sets — "this check was observed red, on this date, by this means (red-then-green / mutation / seeded regression)". Cheap, honest, and it makes the 51 prose paragraphs into something countable.
(c) A REFUSAL — the document proposes reflow2 "refuse to accept a `passing` verification that has never recorded a `failing` run".

🛑 (c) DIRECTLY CONTRADICTS AN ACCEPTED NON-GOAL and must not be built without overturning it. dec:non-goal-reflow2-does-not-judge-whether-a-check-is-meaningful says a passing Verification is a claim reflow2 RECORDS and never one it VALIDATES. Refusing a passing status is reflow2 judging the check. (b) does not cross that line — it records what the author says, exactly like `provenance` and the drift dispositions, and leaves the judging to a human.

HONEST LIMIT, the same one req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause states about itself: this records what the AUTHOR SAYS about their check. It cannot detect a check that was never really red but is claimed to have been. Worth having because the alternative is no signal at all; worth never overselling.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS PROJECT: 42 of this design's checks have never run at all, and nothing distinguishes them from the 188 marked passing in any rollup a user reads. "Passing" and "never able to fail" and "never executed" are three different states wearing one word.
properties.name: OPEN — should a Verification record that it was once observed FAILING, so a check that could never have failed is distinguishable from one that passes? 51 of 191 already say so in prose
properties.rationale: Recorded because the prose count is unusually strong evidence — 51 independent authors' paragraphs working around a missing field is the same measurement that justified the change-event axis, and it was found by reading the graph rather than by reasoning about it. Left open because form (c) contradicts an accepted non-goal, which is Anthony's to overturn or uphold, and because (b) adds vocabulary that will stay empty without the third leg.
